subject: Social Security can now take half your check
preheader: Plus: the 20-minute Medicare check, scammers reading obituaries, and 17 discounts nobody advertises.
greeting: Good morning, and welcome to the first full week of September. Medicare's Annual Notice of Change letters are landing in mailboxes this month, Social Security has quietly moved to a 50% withholding rate on overpayments, and scammers are having a busy fall. We've got a plain-English guide for each.

headline.title: of your monthly Social Security check can now be withheld to recover an overpayment. The old default was 10%.
headline.text: Social Security says it overpaid roughly a million people a year, often because of its own processing delays. Under the rule that took effect in 2025, new overpayments are recovered at half your check unless you act within about 30 days.

stories.why: Three separate forms can lower the withholding, waive the debt entirely, or dispute the amount, and they all work better if you file before the first reduced check goes out.
Plans reprice their drug lists every January. Fifteen minutes on the Medicare Plan Finder is the highest-value chore of the fall for anyone on Part D.
Recently widowed people are the most targeted group in the country, and voice cloning has made the "grandchild in trouble" call frighteningly convincing. Three habits stop nearly all of it.
Readers who start asking "Do you offer a senior discount?" at every register report $30 to $60 a month in savings within weeks.

quiz.q: Under current rules, at what age do required minimum distributions start for someone born in 1962?
quiz.explain: The SECURE 2.0 Act moves the RMD starting age to 75 for anyone born in 1960 or later, beginning in 2033. People born 1951–1959 start at 73.

roundup.text: The new $6,000 senior deduction applies to 2025 returns filed this coming spring, and it phases out above $75,000 of income for single filers.
Open Enrollment runs October 15 through December 7. Your Annual Notice of Change should arrive by September 30.
The lifetime National Parks Senior Pass is still $80 for U.S. citizens 62 and older and covers everyone in your vehicle.
Lifeline takes up to $9.25 a month off phone or internet for anyone on Medicaid, SNAP, or SSI. Most eligible seniors have never applied.
